newsitem.title: CHILE: Enersis to invest $300 mln in Cerj.
newsitem.headline: Enersis to invest $300 mln in Cerj.

text.p: Chilean power investment company Enersis SA will invest $300 million over the next two years in Brazilian electricity firm Cerj to improve service and reduce energy losses, said Enersis CEO Jose Yuraszeck.
Enersis plans to invest a further $200 million in the Rio de Janeiro-based utility in the 1998-2001 period, Juraszeck told a news conference.
"We aim to improve the quality of the service and cut electricity losses, which are running at 28.1 percent," he said.
A statement issued by Enersis at the news conference said that the company would invest $500 million in Cerj in the next five years.
Company officials later clarified this, saying that the investment program would be financed by the whole consortium which includes Spanish and Portuguese firms.

Enersis has 30.6 percent stake and its distribution unit Chilectra acquired a 29.4 percent stake, giving the two a 60 percent presence in the consortium. The bids were placed by two Panamanian companies that are wholly owned by Enersis and Chilectra.
Electricidade de Portugal and Endesa Espana, also in the group, bought 30 percent and 10 percent respectively.
Enersis and its Chilectra distribution unit led the group which bought 70.2 percent of Cerj for 605.3 million reais ($587 million) in an auction today.
The Chilean company, which already has investments in Argentina and Peru, will fund its share of the purchase price and investment plan through its own resources and bank loans, said Yuraszeck.
Payments through privatization bonds will amount to $15 million, he said.
Cerj's electricity prices are fixed for the next eight years and must then be negotiated with the authorities, he said.
"We believe that these rates are adequate," said Yuraszeck.
He said Chilectra, Chile's largest power distributor, will take control of Cerj on November 28.
